intro: A Malian guitarist, son of Ali Farka Touré.
story: Vieux Farka Touré was born in 1981 in Niafunké, Mali, the son of the guitar master Ali Farka Touré. His father discouraged music, so he studied percussion in Bamako while secretly playing guitar. His 2007 debut carried his father's last recorded playing, alongside the kora player Toumani Diabaté, and Fondo followed in 2011; NPR heard a more confident singer and guitarist. He played Pickathon in 2013 and returned in 2023. Les Racines, in 2022 on World Circuit, went back to the desert blues his father played.

story: Shinyribs began as a side project of Kevin Russell of The Gourds, and Russell played Pickathon with it in 2007 and 2008. Gulf Coast Museum, the second album, came out on Nine Mile Records in 2013, after Well After Awhile in 2010, and the Austin Chronicle said it deserved to drop the side-project label. They played Pickathon again in 2013 and 2018. Okra Candy followed in 2015, and The Gourds went on hiatus in late 2013, leaving Russell's side project as his full-time band.
artist_reel_line: Okra Candy came in 2015, after The Gourds went on hiatus in late 2013.

story: The Relatives formed in Dallas in 1970, around the brothers Rev. Gean West and Rev. Tommie West, who fused church harmony with fuzzed-up funk. They faded after the 1970s until the Austin record hunters Noel and Charisse Waggener tracked them down, and a 2009 reunion show at the Continental Club led to The Electric Word on Yep Roc in 2013. They played Pickathon that year, and WNYC recorded a live set. Gean West once said Christ went into the night club and also into hell. He died in February 2015 and Tommie West in March 2024. The Numero Group released the archival album Don't Let Me Fall in January 2025.
artist_reel_line: The Numero Group released the archival album Don't Let Me Fall in 2025.

story: Dale Watson was born in Birmingham, Alabama, in 1962, raised in Pasadena, Texas, and playing professionally by his early teens before he settled in Austin in the mid-1990s. He joined the Austin Music Hall of Fame in 2005 and was named Texas State Musician in 2007. He played Pickathon in 2007, 2009 and 2013, the summer El Rancho Azul took him to the Late Show with David Letterman. In 2014 he founded the Ameripolitan Music Awards, which cover honky tonk, outlaw, western swing and rockabilly. NPR profiled him around Call Me Insane in 2015, and Unwanted, self-produced on Forty Below Records, followed in 2026.
artist_reel_line: Unwanted, self-produced, came out on Forty Below Records.

story: White Fence is the Los Angeles psych-pop project of Tim Presley, formerly of Darker My Love and The Strange Boys, and the first album came out in 2010. Presley released three albums in 2012, among them Family Perfume Vol. 1 and Vol. 2 on Woodsist, and Cyclops Reap, on Castle Face on April 9, 2013, grew from a pile of old leftovers. He played Pickathon that year, and has said that as long as people think it sounds good he does not care how it is labeled. For the Recently Found Innocent followed in 2014. After a step back to paint, Presley returned in 2026 with Orange, the first White Fence album in seven years, on Drag City.
artist_reel_line: Orange, in 2026, was the first White Fence album in seven years.
